system.name: Spectre
system.summary: Package-level architecture contract for the Spectre ecosystem.
notes: A governance layer keeps manifest, validation, and automation concerns separate from runtime packages.

foundation.title: Foundation
foundation.description: Base design-system packages and adapters that higher layers build on.
notes: Foundation packages should remain reusable, framework-light, and safe for broad consumption.

build.title: Build
build.description: Composition and application-facing packages built on top of the foundation layer.

governance.title: Governance
governance.description: Cross-system tooling and contract packages for validation, scaffolding, CI, docs, and AI workflows.
notes: This layer exists so manifest, validation, and automation concerns stay separate from runtime packages.

@phcdevworks/spectre-tokens.description: Design-token source for the Spectre system.

@phcdevworks/spectre-ui.description: Layer 2 styling contract between spectre-tokens and downstream adapters or apps.

@phcdevworks/spectre-components.description: Lit-based component layer of the Spectre system for reusable, accessible, framework-agnostic web components.

@phcdevworks/spectre-ui-astro.description: Astro adapter for the Spectre system for Astro applications that consume the core Spectre UI contract.

@phcdevworks/spectre-shell-router.description: Minimal, framework-agnostic client-side router for Spectre-based applications.

@phcdevworks/spectre-shell-signals.description: Minimal, framework-agnostic reactive primitives package for Spectre applications.

@phcdevworks/spectre-shell.description: Thin, framework-agnostic bootstrap shell for Spectre apps.

@phcdevworks/spectre-base.description: WordPress theme foundation with Vite, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS 4 backed by the Spectre design system.

@phcdevworks/spectre-init.description: Workspace scaffolding entrypoint for creating new Spectre-aligned projects.
notes: If spectre-init starts consuming governance packages later, it should either move into a tooling/governance layer or receive an explicit boundary exception.

@phcdevworks/spectre-manifest.description: Machine-readable contract layer for Spectre tooling, validation, docs, and AI workflows.
notes: This package is consumed by tooling and automation first; runtime packages should not depend on it in v0.1.
Foundation packages may depend on other foundation packages but should not reach upward.
Build packages compose foundation packages and may collaborate within the build layer.
Governance packages stay self-contained so they remain safe for CI, docs, and AI workflows.

forbiddenImports.reason: Foundation must stay reusable and must not depend on composed application packages.
Foundation should not be coupled to tooling or manifest infrastructure.
Build packages are runtime-facing and should not import governance tooling.

boundaryConstraints.rule: Consume and publish through public package exports only; no deep imports across package internals.
boundaryConstraints.reason: Keeps foundation packages stable for adapters and higher-level consumers.

boundaryConstraints.rule: Compose runtime features here, but keep package responsibilities narrow and package-layer ownership explicit.
boundaryConstraints.reason: Prevents shell, routing, signals, components, and theme packages from collapsing into a single grab-bag layer.

boundaryConstraints.rule: Model only system-level and package-level governance in v0.1.
boundaryConstraints.reason: Avoids premature expansion into tokens, component props, routes, or runtime metadata.

preferredEntrypoints.task: Read or validate the Spectre architecture contract
notes: Use this package first for architecture metadata, boundary rules, and safe defaults.
Prefer the scaffolding package over ad hoc repository copying.

preferredEntrypoints.task: Build or consume reusable web components
Build an Astro application with Spectre UI
Build or extend a WordPress theme with Spectre

generationRules: Prefer manifest updates over ad hoc architecture conventions stored only in prose.
Do not introduce dependencies that violate rules.dependencyDirection or package.allowedTargets.
Treat declared package exports as the only supported integration surface.
Assign each package exactly one owning layer and one primary role.
usageGuidance: Read system, layers, and rules before changing package boundaries or adding new packages.
Use the packages registry to discover package responsibilities, consumers, and allowed dependency targets.
When a task touches scaffolding, validation, docs, or AI governance, prefer spectre-manifest or spectre-init before creating bespoke tooling.
safeDefaults: Default new packages to experimental until stability is declared.
Default new internal dependencies to disallowed unless an allowed layer or allowed target explicitly permits them.
Default AI and code generation to public exports only.
Default the canonical manifest file location to /spectre.manifest.json at the repository root.
